lines.t: {P O V=POV}: your {A. I.=AI} agent works perfectly. On your laptop.
Boss says: ship it.
Cool. Now it needs sandboxes. Memory. Auth. Logs. Scaling.
And therapy.
So you duct tape six services together.
Twelve dashboards. Zero sleep.
Prod is on fire. Again.
Meet Amazon Bedrock {agent core=AgentCore}.
Main character: the Harness.
Think restaurant. You bring the recipe. That's your config.
{A W S=AWS} runs the entire kitchen.
A config is a model, tools, skills, and instructions.
Two {A P I=API} calls. {Create Harness=CreateHarness}. {Invoke Harness=InvokeHarness}. That's it.
Built in: a browser, a code interpreter, a shell, and a file system.
Gateway plugs in your {A P Is=APIs} and {M C P=MCP} servers.
{M C P=MCP} is {U S B C=USB-C} for {A. I.=AI} tools.
Memory that remembers you. Unlike your ex.
Any model. Switch mid session, keep the context.
Deploy from the {C L I=CLI}. Now go touch grass.
Now the part that makes other setups sweat.
One. Scale. A hostel crams everyone into one box.
A hotel gives every guest a private, locked room.
One session. One {micro V M=microVM}. Up to eight hours.
Ten sessions or five thousand. Zero servers for you to run.
Two. Security. When a session ends, the {micro V M=microVM} is terminated and memory is wiped.
Your {A P I=API} keys sit in a vault. The agent never sees them.
Three. Observability. Think flight black box.
Session. Trace. Step. Every move recorded.
Versus you, at {three A M=3AM}, hopping between log groups.
Pricing. You pay for active {C P U=CPU}.
Waiting on the model? No {C P U=CPU} billed.
The harness fee? Zero dollars.
Ops is built in. Versions. Rollbacks. Evals. {A B=A/B} tests.
Outgrow config? Export to code. Keep your model, prompt, and tools.
Scoreboard. {D I Y=DIY} stack versus {agent core=AgentCore} Harness.
Setup. Scale. Security. Observability.
Not even close.
Your job is shipping agents. Not babysitting infrastructure.
Go build.
